title: Give departments back the capital moved to defence
name: Give departments back the capital moved to defence
noun: undoing the capital moved to defence
headline: Undo the defence capital move. Costs £1.1bn in 2029-30.
description: The Budget funds the last £4.7 billion of the Defence Investment Plan by moving capital from other departments’ budgets, cutting them by 1% from 2027-28. Switch this on to give that capital back and borrow for the plan instead. Capital, so it counts against the debt rule.

baselinePolicy.text: Capital is reallocated from other departments to fully fund the Defence Investment Plan (Table 6.1 line 41); the plan’s own spending is line 40.

source.quote: This Budget confirms that the residual £4.7 billion will be funded through reprioritisation of capital budgets.

alreadyIncludes: Capital is reallocated from other departments to fully fund the Defence Investment Plan (Table 6.1 line 41); the plan’s own spending is line 40.

lines.title: Defence Investment Plan: Reallocate capital spending to fully fund the Defence Investment Plan

rawSource.note: Reversal on the spending side: the Treasury’s costing with the sign kept (a line that reduced borrowing is spending the reversal adds back; a line that cost money is spending the reversal saves).

caveats: The Treasury’s costing is on the OBR October 2026 forecast, the baseline used here. Effects before the start year are not applied: 2026-27 falls before any Budget of yours.
This undoes the funding, not the plan: defence keeps its money either way, and the other departments get theirs back.

considerations.text: The Treasury’s scorecard figure is the Budget’s own costing of the measure, certified by the OBR as part of its October 2026 forecast.
